content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] with digital and analog inputs. What is the minimum voltage required for a valid digital input?
signal status = 0 for less than 5V; signal status = 1 for greater than 8V. Refer to the manual edition 05/2006, page 32.

For a [product_name], the input considered as '1' must be higher than 8.5V. What is the maximum DC voltage allowed? I want to use 24VDC as a digital input and am concerned about exceeding the rated input.
The [product_name] can accept 24V at any input.
You can find the parameters for input voltage values in the attached file.

Here's a tip for detecting digital signals below the usual threshold: If you need to detect a lower voltage (for example, 3V), this is not feasible with a standard digital input. In such cases, use an analog input with an analog threshold trigger. Set the ON threshold to 30 (which represents 3V for a 0-10V sensor). Be sure to set the appropriate OFF threshold (hysteresis) to prevent unwanted toggling. This provides a way to detect signals below the standard digital input threshold. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for clarity regarding the voltage requirements for digital inputs on a specific [product_name] device, including both the minimum activation voltage and maximum safe voltage. The discussion shows uncertainty and highlights the need for clearer product specifications, especially for scenarios involving voltages near the threshold or below it. Suggestions for workarounds, such as using analog inputs and threshold triggers, also emerge.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to receive straightforward and reliable guidance on the voltage limits for digital inputs, including assurance that using 24VDC as a digital input will not harm the device.
